pr_body:
Closes #3809 
This PR adds base support for theming, and selecting themes.
Not to be confused with light/dark themes, as these themes can utilize both.

You can test this by adding themes to the themes folder that should be created when you run the branch.

Themes are in the form of xaml files with resource dictionaries.

Basic example of theming:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/59544401/110368349-c7c59400-7ffd-11eb-99c4-e370eb424798.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/59544401/110368587-18d58800-7ffe-11eb-99b6-6a3234ed5f86.png)

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When using custom themes for windows, or custom themes in general, you are unable to manually change the color values of the Files app.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I would like a hidden/experimental settings panel from which you could change the hex values of the app.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Another solution would be a config file from which you could change the hex values of the app.

**Additional context**
Edit: I know this is similar to #3176, but I believe this to not be a duplicate because in #3176, the author wants support for custom explorer themes, whereas I want a way to manually change the color codes via a gui or a config file.
comments:
@yaichenbaum 
The main thing I would like with theming is the ability to customize the look of Files overall (margins, sizing, padding, etc.), not just the colors.

For example, I really dont like thin grid splitters, because I have big fingers so they're really hard to use on a touch screen. Since this is not an issue for most users, it doesn't really make sense to widen it in the Files codebase. It would be nice to have an easy way to customize the grid splitter template.

I think a solid way to do this would be to allow loading xaml resource dictionaries.
This gives a simple way to change the color scheme of Files, and also allows for more advanced configuration like re-templating controls.

This approach would, for example, allow me to increase the size of the grid splitters.

There are also theming utilities like [Fluent Xaml Theme Editor](https://github.com/microsoft/fluent-xaml-theme-editor) that could be used to design themes and generate the resources. Or, Files could have a built-in one.

I have a working prototype of this, if you're interested. 
You can add a theme dictionary to ```%userprofile%\AppData\Local\Packages\FilesDev_et10x9a9vyk8t\LocalState\themes```
https://github.com/winston-de/Files/tree/Theming

---
- How will custom themes add value to your usage of Files?

This would make it much easier to tailor Files to my own needs and address some personal pain points.

- Are you looking for the option to edit the brushes used inside Files?

Yes

- Are you looking for the option to edit font colors as well?

Yes

- Are you looking for a couple of themes to be built into Files?

I think a sample/template built in would be nice for reference.
Also, perhaps compact mode could be done by having a compact and standard theme installed by default.
@MudkipBanana @winston-de This issue has been approved for further development, at the moment, the plan is to detect custom resource files and load them in Files.
This issue should be resolved with #3890.
